:::{#exm-median-survival-cure}
#### A survival function with no finite median (counterexample)

Suppose 60% of patients are cured and never experience the event,
while the other 40% have exponentially distributed event times with rate $\haz = 1$ per year,
so that
$\surv(t) = 0.6 + 0.4\,\ef{-t}$.
To find $t_{\text{med}}$ (@def-median-survival),
we look for times $t$ with $\surv(t) \le 0.5$:

$$
\ba
\surv(t) \le 0.5
&\iff 0.6 + 0.4\,\ef{-t} \le 0.5
&& \text{(substitute $\surv(t)$)}
\\
&\iff 0.4\,\ef{-t} \le -0.1
&& \text{(subtract 0.6 from both sides)}
\\
&\iff \ef{-t} \le -0.25
&& \text{(divide both sides by $0.4 > 0$)}
\ea
$$

No $t$ satisfies $\ef{-t} \le -0.25$, because $\ef{-t} > 0$ for every $t$.
The set $\cb{t \ge 0 : \surv(t) \le 0.5}$ is empty,
so this population has no finite [median survival time](#def-median-survival)
(by the convention $\inf \emptyset = \infty$, $t_{\text{med}} = \infty$).
:::
